KYC/AML Compliance Guide for Security Token Offerings

By Sails.to Team • January 22, 2026 • 14 min read

Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) compliance aren't optional for security tokens. They're foundational requirements that protect issuers, investors, and the integrity of compliant digital asset markets.

Why KYC/AML Matters for Security Tokens

Legal Requirement

Securities offerings—whether traditional or tokenized—require investor verification. For Reg D 506(c) offerings, issuers must take "reasonable steps" to verify accredited investor status. For Reg S, you must confirm non-US person status.

Real Estate Tokenization: Unlocking Liquidity in Illiquid Markets

By Sails.to Team • January 20, 2026 • 11 min read

Commercial real estate is a $20+ trillion market with one persistent problem: illiquidity. Properties take months to sell, ownership requires significant capital, and global investors face friction entering local markets. Tokenization changes all of that.

The Illiquidity Problem

Traditional commercial real estate investing works like this:

  • Minimum investments of $250K–$1M+ for direct ownership
  • Complex legal structures requiring attorney involvement
  • Sale processes taking 6–12 months
  • Limited access to international capital
  • Paper-based cap tables and manual distributions

This illiquidity creates an "illiquidity discount"—investors pay less because they can't easily exit. Estimates suggest 20–30% value erosion compared to liquid alternatives.

Why Wyoming? The State Leading Crypto Innovation

By Sails.to Team • January 15, 2026 • 8 min read

When we decided to build Sails.to, one of our first decisions was where to incorporate. We chose Wyoming—and it wasn't just because of the scenery. Wyoming has quietly become the most crypto-friendly jurisdiction in the United States, passing over 30 blockchain-enabling laws since 2018.

The Wyoming Advantage

Wyoming offers something no other state does: legal recognition of DAOs as limited liability companies. This isn't a workaround or a gray area—it's explicit statute, signed into law in 2021.

Security Tokens Explained: What They Are and Why They Matter

By Sails.to Team • January 10, 2026 • 10 min read

If you've heard about cryptocurrency, you've probably encountered terms like "utility tokens," "NFTs," and "DeFi." But security tokens are different—and potentially more important for the future of finance.

What Is a Security Token?

A security token is a digital representation of a traditional financial security—stocks, bonds, fund shares, or real estate interests—issued on a blockchain. Unlike cryptocurrency, security tokens are subject to securities regulations and represent actual ownership in real assets.
